questions.q: According to this lesson, what three things must eradication remove to actually be complete?
options: The attacker's tooling, the root-cause vulnerability that allowed access, and any persistence mechanisms planted while the attacker was inside
Only the malware that triggered the original alert
Only the user account the attacker initially phished
Nothing beyond what an antivirus scan flags as malicious
questions.explain: Eradication is three jobs, not one: remove the attacker's tooling, close the vulnerability that let them in, and remove every persistence mechanism they planted.

questions.q: In the Meridian Outpatient Billing scenario, what is the actual root cause of the incident, as opposed to a symptom of it?
options: The unpatched Remote Desktop Gateway server that gave the attacker initial access
The svc-helpdesk local administrator account
The SystemHealthCheck scheduled task
The WinHealthSvc registry Run key entry
questions.explain: The svc-helpdesk account, the scheduled task, and the registry entry are all things the attacker planted after getting in — the missing security update on the RD Gateway is how they got in, which makes it the root cause.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend running Get-ScheduledTask before Unregister-ScheduledTask when removing a suspicious scheduled task?
options: To confirm the task and its action before deleting it, so a legitimate scheduled job isn't removed by mistake
Get-ScheduledTask is required to grant permission to delete the task
Unregister-ScheduledTask does not work unless Get-ScheduledTask has run first in the same session
To automatically patch the vulnerability that allowed the task to be created
questions.explain: Deleting blind risks removing something legitimate; confirming what a task actually does first is the safer sequence.

questions.q: What is the purpose of cross-checking Event ID 4720 and Event ID 4698 across every host in scope during eradication?
options: To confirm no additional rogue account or scheduled task was created elsewhere that hasn't been found and removed yet
To automatically remove malware without any manual steps
To patch the Remote Desktop Gateway vulnerability
To restart affected servers after cleanup
questions.explain: Event ID 4720 logs new local account creation and 4698 logs new scheduled task creation; checking every host for these events helps confirm no fourth foothold was missed.

questions.q: Why would removing Meridian's svc-helpdesk account and SystemHealthCheck scheduled task, without patching the Remote Desktop Gateway, leave the incident unresolved?
options: The missing security update that allowed initial access would still be there, letting the same or a different attacker back in the same way
Local accounts cannot actually be deleted with PowerShell
Scheduled tasks automatically recreate themselves on any Windows server
The registry Run key alone caused the entire compromise
questions.explain: Cleaning up what the attacker planted doesn't close the door they walked through; the root-cause vulnerability has to be patched too.
